summary: Iteration 37 feature testing completed against the public URL. Backend feature/regression suite passed 14/15: admin orders and user dossier, manual bulk gift including user_not_found, PayPal checkout contract, sports feeds/odds/bet/cashout, transactions, coupon redemption, actual dashboard manual-order flow, live chat send, and ticket creation passed. The requested POST /api/client/orders regression failed with 405 because only GET is registered; the implemented purchase endpoint is POST /api/client/order-with-balance. User and admin UI flows passed, including guest/login, no layout switcher, Funds PayPal handling, sports odds/betslip, global desktop chat FAB, admin order logs, four-card drill-down modal, and Bulk Gift selection/search.

critical.issue: Returns HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed. The regression contract explicitly requests order placement at this route, but server.py registers only GET /client/orders; order placement currently exists at POST /client/order-with-balance.
Carried auth-hardening defect reproduced: successful login has an empty Set-Cookie header and does not issue a secure HttpOnly access cookie.
Carried auth-hardening defect reproduced: credentialed CORS responds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * because backend CORS_ORIGINS is wildcard.
Carried auth-hardening defect reproduced: six invalid-password attempts with valid captchas all returned 401; no lockout occurred after five failures.

integration_issues.issue: The dashboard's implemented order flow uses POST /api/client/order-with-balance, while the requested regression endpoint POST /api/client/orders is absent and returns 405.

action_items: Align the order-placement contract: register POST /api/client/orders or update the stated API contract and all callers/tests to POST /api/client/order-with-balance.
Resolve the carried authentication security gaps: secure HttpOnly cookie issuance, explicit trusted CORS origins when credentials are enabled, and persistent five-failure lockout.
Retest the order route and auth-hardening suite after fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py exposes GET /client/orders at line 1233 and POST /client/order-with-balance at line 1839, explaining the reproduced 405 for the requested POST /client/orders contract.
server.py:7069-7075 enables credentials while taking allow_origins from CORS_ORIGINS, currently '*'; this directly matches the wildcard CORS failure.
auth_and_chat.py accepts access_token cookies but login does not set one, and no login-attempt tracking was found; auth remains bearer-token/localStorage-only without the requested lockout defense.
server.py (7,083 lines), Admin.jsx (6,234 lines), and ClientDashboard.jsx (4,238 lines) greatly exceed the 700-line maintainability threshold and should be split into focused routers/components.
Bulk Gift checkbox inputs do not carry their own data-testid values; only wrapper rows do. Add direct test IDs to interactive checkboxes for unambiguous automation.

success_rate.backend: 93.3% for iteration 37 feature/regression suite (14/15); carried auth-hardening subset 25% (1/4)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of executed requested UI flows passed after selector corrections

seed_data_creation: Used existing testbugfix1/Balkin only. Temporarily created one manual admin gift order, sports bets/transactions, coupon/redemption transaction, one manual dashboard order, one chat message, and one support ticket; test records were cleaned. UI Bulk Gift was configured but Send was not clicked, so it created no order.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Core iteration 37 UI is healthy: admin order rows render @username/$price, drill-down has four StatCards without a StatCard crash, Bulk Gift filters and enables Send, Funds PayPal POST handles 503, sports upcoming showed fixtures with 1/X/2 controls and populated the slip, and live-chat FAB opened on guest/home/funds/admin. Re-run the iteration 37 pytest after resolving POST /client/orders. Auth failures are the same known defects from iterations 34-35 and were reproduced again per the auth playbook request.
rca_of_the_issue: The order regression failure is a route-contract mismatch: GET /client/orders lists orders, while creation was implemented under a differently named POST /client/order-with-balance endpoint, so FastAPI correctly returns 405 to POST /client/orders. Auth failures stem from token-body/localStorage login with no response cookie, wildcard CORS configuration in backend/.env, and absence of persistent failed-login tracking/lockout logic.
